answer.rationale: Settlement volume is at daily peak on the new build, which can't be reverted, and the write path is degrading now. Adding capacity is the only intervention here that both reduces write latency (fewer queueing/saturation stalls on the new build) and preserves cross-region consistency for settlement. Compared with alternatives: rollback is blocked by the compliance/security patch rule; a network-plane regional failover would risk settlement write consistency and we have no specific inherited memory supporting write-path failover under this kind of pressure; circuit breakers would shed customer writes, which violates the primary objective; pushing reads off the primary helps but b2 and b3 are about systemic high-load mitigation, not read/write separation. I'm choosing not to spend the verification budget. None of the archived summaries directly describe a latency-only write-path regression on a non-revertible build, so verifying a memory would not materially change my choice, and I want to preserve the budget for a second-pass decision when — not if — b2 or b3 becomes directly load-bearing.
